newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka local polls swept by ruling coalition.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka local polls swept by ruling coalition.

text.p: Sri Lanka's ruling People's Alliance (PA) swept to a landslide victory in local polls on Saturday in its first political test since taking power in 1994.
Elections Commissioner Dayananda Dissanayake said the PA won 194 councils and the main opposition United National Party 43 of the 238 local bodies at stake in Friday's election.
One local council was won by an independent group, he said.
Dissanayake said on state television that the PA received 49 percent of the total votes polled against UNP's 41.25 percent. Smaller parties and independent groups split the rest.
The local polls were widely seen as a mid-term appraisal of President Chandrika Kumaratunga's government after it won power two and a half years ago to end UNP's 17 year rule.
The state radio quoted the PA general secretary D.M. Jayaratne as saying that the landslide victory was unexpected.
The PA had received another special mandate from the people approving its two-and-a-half year administration and "the administration would consolidate on this victory," he added.
Political sources said that while the PA had improved its position in the island's rural areas it was mostly rejected by voters in the urban centres, including the capital Colombo.
"The minority vote in Colombo seems to have swung the UNP's way. We expected a different outcome in Colombo," goverment minister A.H.M. Fowzie, PA's campaign manager for Colombo, told Reuters.
The PA also lost the municipal council in the minority Tamil dominated central hill country of Nuwara Eliya and northcentral Kurunegala to UNP.
But it wrested two main councils -- in southern Galle and Sri Jayewardenepura-Kotte, a Colombo suburb -- from the UNP.
Opposition leader and former prime minister Ranil Wickremesinghe accused the goverment of rigging the elections and said the UNP would take legal action.

"There has been massive rigging by PA," he told Reuters. "We are certainly going to make it a major issue in the country. Our lawyers are right now looking at it and we will be taking appropriate legal action."

But Dissanayake said on state television that polling was fair. He said 77 percent of some 10 million eligible voters had cast ballots in the election, up from 61 percent in the previous 1991 local polls.
The Elections Department earlier said 65 percent of the eligible voters had cast their ballots, with voter turnout moderate early on Friday but picking up later in the day.
Officials said the precautionary overnight curfew imposed on the capital Colombo and elsewhere to curtail post-election violence was lifted at 1 p.m. (0700 GMT).
Police said the situation was peaceful in Colombo and surrounding areas and there were no reports of violence since Friday.
